html:
The Kolla and Atacameño are Indigenous peoples of the high, dry puna of north-western Argentina and northern Chile, around the Atacama Desert. The Atacameño, or Lickanantay, lived in oases such as San Pedro de Atacama and spoke Kunza, a language that died out in the 1900s. The Kolla are the Andean people of the Argentine highlands.

They farmed in irrigated oases, herded llamas and alpacas, and ran llama caravans that carried goods between the Pacific coast, the high plateau and the eastern valleys. San Pedro had ties to Tiwanaku centuries before. In the late 1400s the Inca Empire took over the region, and after 1536 the Spanish. Their neighbours included the Diaguita to the south and the Omaguaca to the east.
